hero.h1: The execution layer between intent and markets.
hero.lead: Send a trade intent. Suwappu ranks every venue, shows the route, and executes only when you approve. Trade through Terminal, Telegram, or the API.
hero.byline_mid: - a hands-on DeFi-security book, and an open-source contributor to

hero.eyebrow: For traders, trading teams, and AI agents
hero.lead: Quote any route across DEXs and bridges, see which venue won and why, and move funds only after you authorize. One engine runs the Terminal, Telegram, and the Agent API.

interfaces.title: Built for traders, teams, and the agents they run.
interfaces.lead: Trade by hand in the Terminal or Telegram. Put the same engine inside your product with REST, MCP, and SDKs.
interfaces.boundary: Each surface carries its own authority. MCP tools prepare unsigned transactions and never broadcast them. Managed signing is a separate REST path, and A2A stops at quoting.

execution.title: Every trade is quoted, explained, and authorized.
execution.lead: Routing and authority are separate decisions. Get a quote, run an optional dry run, then authorize.
execution.intentBody: Specify amount, assets, source, and destination. Nothing has moved yet.
execution.quoteBody: Only venues that support the requested chains and pair compete. The response names the route that won.
execution.simulateBody: Optional. The Agent API can dry-run the proposed swap and its safety checks without signing or moving funds.
execution.authorizeBody: Self-custody returns an unsigned transaction for you to sign. Managed execution signs and broadcasts under server-side policy.
execution.screenshotAlt: Suwappu Terminal showing an ETH/USDC chart, order book, and swap ticket.
execution.mevBody: An in-house searcher, written in Rust, screens each route for sandwich risk before it executes.
execution.benchBody: Every execution path is benchmarked on real latency and slippage.

proof.mobileHint: Product screenshot. On narrow screens, scroll horizontally to inspect full-size interface detail.

markets.title: Routes are chosen on price and on reliability.
markets.crossChainBody: Spot execution across {platformChains} chains in the product and {agentApiChains} through the Agent API. Each quote draws only on venues that can serve that route.
markets.hyperliquidBody: Trade HyperLiquid perpetuals and spot from Suwappu's product surfaces. Programmatic access depends on the Agent API or MCP tool you use.
markets.tempoBody: Tempo's enshrined DEX is part of the routing set. Through the Agent API, Tempo covers token discovery today, and swap execution is not yet enabled.
markets.curveBody: The terminal's Curve venue lists every pool on every chain Curve deploys to, straight from the Curve Prices API. Sort by TVL, 24h volume or base APR, search it, and reach the swap desk in one click. Built on our fork of flet-curve.
markets.screenshotAlt: Suwappu perps desk showing HyperLiquid markets, market data, and an order ticket.
markets.screenshotCaption: HyperLiquid perps inside Suwappu · product capture · 31 Jul 2026
markets.lead: Tempo's enshrined DEX, CoW's batch auctions, and bridge settlement all feed one ranking. If a provider degrades, failover keeps the route available.

security.title: Self-custody or managed. Your rules either way.
security.lead: Sign every transaction yourself, or let a managed wallet sign within limits you set.
security.selfCustodyBody: Unsigned transaction flows leave signing and broadcasting with you. No server ever holds that key.
security.managedBody: Managed wallets sign through KMS envelope encryption, Turnkey's trusted execution environment, or an MPC signer, depending on the wallet.
security.policiesBody: 2FA, spending limits, circuit breakers, and social recovery are enforced on the server. Approval monitoring revokes the token approvals it flags.
security.boundaryBody: Suwappu does not yet hold SOC 2 certification or a completed public protocol audit. The security page lists the controls in place today and what remains open.

limits.title: Precise claims you can plan around.
limits.lead: Four boundaries worth knowing before you route production volume.
limits.venuesTitle: Not every venue competes for every quote.
limits.venuesBody: Venue support varies by chain and by route. Suwappu evaluates the compatible subset and shows which route it selected.
limits.bestExTitle: A quote is not best execution.
limits.bestExBody: The route is selected on the evidence available at quote time. Realized cost is measured after the fact, and we publish the method rather than claiming the outcome.
limits.agentsTitle: Agent tools prepare, they do not spend.
limits.agentsBody: The MCP swap tool returns an unsigned transaction. Managed execution is a separate, explicit path with its own authorization.
limits.postQuantumTitle: Post-quantum work is built, not certified.
limits.postQuantumBody: The Lattice Transfer Protocol is built toward FedRAMP High readiness. It does not hold that authorization today.

faq.title: The practical questions, answered plainly.
faq.coverageQuestion: What does the platform actually cover?
faq.coverageAnswer: The platform covers {platformChains} chains and {routerCount} integrated routing venues. The Agent API exposes {agentApiChains} chains today, and every route uses only the venues that support it.
faq.venuesQuestion: Do all {routerCount} venues compete for every quote?
faq.venuesAnswer: No. Venue support varies by chain and route. Suwappu evaluates the compatible subset and exposes the selected route.
faq.authorityAnswer: Self-custody flows return unsigned transactions for the caller to sign. Managed REST execution can sign and broadcast through a managed wallet under server-side controls.
faq.interfacesQuestion: Do REST, MCP, and A2A have the same authority?
faq.interfacesAnswer: No. REST covers both managed and self-custody execution. MCP's execute_swap prepares an unsigned transaction and never broadcasts it. A2A stops at discovery and quoting.

portfolio.title: One book for a position that spans chains.
portfolio.lead: Positions roll up across every chain the terminal trades, into one book you can read at a glance. A weekly digest recaps performance.
portfolio.positionsBody: One positions service aggregates holdings across every supported chain, no per-chain bookkeeping.
portfolio.pnlBody: PnL is computed per position and rolled into a single equity curve in the Terminal.
portfolio.cardsBody: A position can mint an on-chain receipt: a position card that travels with the trade.

government.title: Post-quantum data transfer for the public sector.
government.lead: The Lattice Transfer Protocol handles post-quantum data transfer with on-chain anchors. It is built toward FedRAMP High readiness, not yet certified.
government.pqBody: Standard mode uses ML-KEM-768 (FIPS 203) key encapsulation, ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signatures, and BLAKE3 content addressing.
government.provenBody: Lean 4 proofs cover quorum safety, constant-size sealed keys, and erasure thresholds, gated in CI.
government.fedrampBody: An evidence package with a NIST SP 800-53 control crosswalk and a fail-closed government deployment profile.
